note: Route tags classify the kind of record a lead concerns; they are not findings of fact, liability or legal merit. A lead may appear on more than one route. A public-body tag identifies an institutional record or actor only; it is not, by itself, a ground to set aside the 1987 judgment. Route gauges show the highest evidence-held score among tagged leads, not a probability or percentage chance. For the 1982–83 applications, use the Land Registration Act 1925 and Rules then in force: do not apply the later Land Registration Rules 2003 rule 28 / Form DI retrospectively. The original Forms 1C/1E and any section 14 declaration actually required by the Registrar must be read before alleging a false answer. Under section 70(1)(g) of the 1925 Act, a pre-existing right held by a person in actual occupation could remain overriding on first registration; actual occupation alone did not create ownership. Section 14 required an applicant/solicitor declaration only if the Registrar required it, and section 53 gave notice to a qualifying cautioner. The 2003 Form DI duty is later.

routes.label: Dishonesty
routes.desc: A document, signature or statement relevant to an enquiry into possible dishonesty. The tag is a research category, not a finding that dishonesty occurred.

routes.label: Concealment
routes.desc: A record relevant to an enquiry into possible non-production, non-disclosure or loss. The tag does not establish deliberate concealment.

routes.label: Public bodies
routes.desc: A record made, held or dealt with by a registry, court, council or other public body. This is a separate institutional enquiry route, not a ground to reopen the 1987 judgment on its own.
